## Summary

Rewrote `lib/browserUtils/scrollToBottom.js`:
- Replaced the single before/after `scrollHeight` comparison with a counter requiring `stableRounds` (default 3) consecutive unchanged height readings before declaring "reached bottom", with a `checkDelay` (default 300ms) wait after each scroll step for lazy content to land.
- Added `maxScrolls` (default 100) as a hard cap independent of `timeout`, since a long `checkDelay` could otherwise let the loop run for a very long time even under a generous timeout.
- Each default is justified in a code comment explaining the three-way tradeoff (short delay → false "done"; low cap → missed content; high cap → slow scrape), not picked arbitrarily.
- Height reads re-resolve the scroll container every round, with `containerSelector` as an opt-in override; a missing/removed container falls back to the page instead of throwing.
- Handles height dropping then recovering (resets the stable-streak instead of misreading it as "done") and container removal mid-scroll (try/catch around read/scroll, loop always exits via the hard caps, never hangs or throws out of `page.evaluate`).

Updated `lib/index.js` to pass through the new options (`stableRounds`, `checkDelay`, `maxScrolls`, `containerSelector`) from the existing `scrollToBottom` config object, and documented them in README.md.

Added `test/scrollToBottom.test.js` (7 cases) plus a new mock page `test/mock/lazy-load.html` that inserts items in waves after scroll, covering: waiting out async batches, failing-fast with too-short `checkDelay` (pins the original bug), hard exit at `timeout`, hard exit at `maxScrolls`, height-drop-then-recover, and container removed/missing mid-scroll.

Ran `npm install` then `npm test`: all 51 tests pass, including the full existing `test/puppeteer-plugin.test.js` integration suite and the new unit tests.
